parsedVerdict.reasoning: The controller does normal presentation-layer work. It declares routes (@Controller, @Post, @Delete), applies auth and permission guards, binds the request body and route params, and maps a missing resource to an HTTP 403 via HttpException. Everything else is passed to application services (AccountService, AccountBalanceService). It contains no direct persistence calls, no domain calculations and no business rules beyond a request-scoped ownership check. That check is just a lookup scoped by userId, and placing it in the controller is acceptable access control at the transport boundary. One minor point: the Prisma composite-key filter shape (`id_userId`) is passed through accountService.account(), which leaks a persistence-shaped query detail into the controller. But this is a parameter to a service call, not persistence logic run by the controller, so it does not amount to a misplaced responsibility under this rubric.
